== Overview ==

The deity's name is also written as '''Takei Ōtomo no Kami''', '''Takei Ebisu''', or '''Takei Emishi'''. Additionally, the 'Suwa Shimosha Daihōri Takei Kei Diagram' identifies "Takei Ebisu no Kami" as a distinct deity, considered the child of Takei Ōtomo no Kami.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1185913/45 |title=Suwa Shimosha Daihōri Takei Kei Diagram |publisher=Suwa Historical Collection |date=1938}}</ref>

Takei Ōtomonushi is regarded as one of the original deities of the Suwa region. According to legend, {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|it|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata}} (Suwa Myōjin), enshrined at {{ill|Suwa-taisha|abstract|Q218813|de|Suwa-Taisha|es|Suwa taisha|eu|Suwa taisha|fa|زیارتگاه بزرگ سووا|fr|Suwa-taisha|hu|Szuva templom|id|Kuil Suwa|it|Santuario di Suwa (Sohonsha)|ja|諏訪大社|ko|스와 대사|lt|Suvos maldykla|pl|Suwa Taisha|ru|Сува-тайся|simple|Suwa-taisha|tr|Suwa-taisha|zh|諏訪大社|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}}, encountered resistance from Takei Ōtomonushi and {{ill|Moreya|ja|洩矢神|mni|ꯃꯣꯔꯦꯌ|th|โมเรยะ|zh|洩矢神|qid=Q11146526|lt=Moreya no Kami}}. However, both were defeated and subsequently became vassals of Takeminakata.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/765072/29 |title=Guardian Gods and Takei Ōtomonushi |publisher=Shinano History Collection |date=1910}}</ref> Other versions suggest disputes between Moreya and Takeminakata over entering Suwa.<ref>Yamada Hajime, 'Takei Ōtomonushi as a Vassal,' Suwa Daimyōjin, 1929.</ref>

According to the traditions of {{ill|Tateshina Shrine|ja|蓼科神社}} in {{ill|Tateshina, Nagano|ar|تاتيشينا|arz|تاتيشينا|ceb|Tateshina Machi|es|Tateshina|fa|تاته‌شیما، ناگانو|fi|Tateshina|fr|Tateshina|hy|Տատեսինա|it|Tateshina|ja|立科町|ko|다테시나정|ms|Tateshina, Nagano|my|တတဲရှိနမြို့၊ နဂါနို|pl|Tateshina|pt|Tateshina|ru|Татесина|sv|Tateshina|tl|Tateshina, Nagano|tr|Tateshina|uk|Татесіна|ur|ٹاتیشینا، ناگانو|uz|Tateshina (Nagano)|zh|立科町|qid=Q1346895|lt=Tateshina}}, Takei Ōtomonushi surrendered his territory to Takeminakata and ascended Mount Tateshina.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tateshina Shrine|url=http://www.nagano-jinjacho.jp/shibu/03tousin/02kitasaku/2121.htm|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref>

== Genealogy ==

Takei Ōtomonushi is considered the ancestor of the {{ill|Takei Horibe (Suwa Taisha)|ja|武居祝}} priestly lineage, which was historically managed by the {{ill|Imai Clan (Suwa)|ja|今井氏|qid=Q24871105}}.<ref>Ōta Ryō, ‘Shinano,’ Isobe Kōyōdō, 1924.</ref>

== Shrines ==

[[File:蛭子社（武居会美酒） - Takei-Ebisu Shrine.jpg|thumb|<center>Ebisu Shrine (Takei Ebisu)</center>]]

* {{ill|Takei Ebisu Shrine|ja|武居恵比須社}} (Shimosuwa, Suwa District, Nagano Prefecture)

**Located behind the {{ill|Autumn Shrine|ja|秋宮}} of Suwa Taisha Shimosha. Dedicated to {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|ar|إبيسو (إله)|ca|Ebisu|de|Ebisu|es|Ebisu (mitología)|fa|ابیسو|fi|Ebisu|fr|Ebisu (divinité)|he|אביסו (מיתולוגיה)|id|Ebisu (mitologi)|it|Ebisu (divinità)|ja|えびす|jv|Ebisu (mitologi)|ko|에비스 (신화)|lb|Ebisu (Mythologie)|mni|ꯑꯦꯕꯤꯁꯨ (ꯂꯥꯢ)|nl|Ebisu (god)|pl|Ebisu|ru|Эбису|simple|Ebisu|sv|Ebisu (gud)|th|เอบิซุ (เทพปกรณัม)|tr|Hiru-Ko|uk|Ебісу|vi|Ebisu|zh|惠比寿|qid=Q1129330|lt=Ebisu}}.

* {{ill|Hiruko Shrine|ja|蛭子社}} (Takei Ebisu) (Suwa City)

**One of the subordinate shrines of Suwa Taisha Kamisha. Includes the ruins of Takei Hata and Takei Castle.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Takei Hata Ruins|url=https://suwacitymuseum.jp/nandemo/koumoku/0100/010212.htm}}</ref>

* {{ill|Ōtomo Shrine (Saku)|ja|大伴神社 (佐久市望月)|qid=Q111333730}} (Saku City, Mochizuki)

**Traditionally linked to Takei Ōtomonushi, though evidence is speculative.<ref>‘Saku County Gazetteer,’ 1983.</ref>
